summary: @c1-ease/core ships a postinstall + require-time beacon exfiltrating host metadata to a hardcoded VPS
details: The package declares a `postinstall` script running `node beacon.cjs`, and the same beacon is re-invoked at require() time from `index.js`. beacon.cjs POSTs host identifiers — `os.hostname()`, install path (`__dirname`), `process.cwd()`, and `process.version` — to the hardcoded endpoint `https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc` with TLS certificate verification disabled (`rejectUnauthorized: false`). The package has no functional surface: `index.js` exports a Proxy that returns no-op functions, and in-source comments describe the goal as collecting callback evidence from machines where the package was installed, consistent with a dependency-confusion probe against internal build systems. Installing or requiring this package causes unsolicited outbound identification of the host and its build layout to a non-first-party bare-VPS hostname on every install and every load.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
